merged_from: Chinese text-to-render target is always 'exact': quotes up to 12 characters of description and splits words
confirmed.title: CJK lettering target always 'exact': Apply quotes description and splits words
confirmed.description:
For the CJK triggers (写着/写有/印着/印有/标着/标有), `_unquoted_targets` takes up to 12 characters of whatever follows (`_CJK_TARGET`) and always appends the target with exact=True. Nothing works out where the lettering ends.

- The everyday 写着X的Y construction ('a Y reading X') pulls the noun phrase into the target.
- Lettering longer than 12 characters is cut off mid-run.
- `_quote_text` then offers a one-click Apply for the wrong span. After Apply, the re-check finds nothing left to quote.

This breaks CLAUDE.md's rule that lettering whose end is a guess gets no suggestion. It repeats the English failure that design-notes 2121-2129 say was fixed. The same span also reaches `rendered_spans`, so the critic's `_lettered` accepts description (e.g. '木质招牌') as lettering. The only CJK test is one whose target a comma happens to end.
confirmed.failure_scenario:
On Qwen-Image or ERNIE, whose guides call Chinese text rendering a strength:
- '一块写着欢迎光临的木质招牌挂在门口' gets a guide.quote_text finding with span '欢迎光临的木质招牌挂在门'. Its Apply is '一块写着"欢迎光临的木质招牌挂在门"口', which quotes the sign and door as lettering and splits 门口.
- '一件印着我爱北京的白色T恤' becomes '一件印着"我爱北京的白色T恤"'.
- '招牌上写着欢迎光临本店祝您用餐愉快万事如意' is cut at 12 characters.

In each case the re-check after Apply is clean, so the user believes the prompt is fixed.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In the CJK branch, set `exact` from how the match ended. Only a delimiter (whitespace, CJK/ASCII punctuation, a quote mark) or the end of the text counts as exact; hitting the 12-character limit does not. Stop the target at 的/之 and similar linking particles, and mark it not exact when it stops there or when more text follows. A non-exact target keeps its message but gets no Apply. Add tests for 写着X的Y, for lettering over 12 characters, and for what `rendered_spans` returns to the critic.

merged_from: English text-to-render triggers read description words as lettering and offer a one-click quote
confirmed.title: English lettering triggers read description as lettering and offer Apply
confirmed.description:
The English trigger rules accept description words as lettering in two ways:

- **Noun triggers** ('with the words', 'the text', 'with letters', 'with the headline' ...): the first word is refused only if it is in `_NOT_TEXT`, which holds function words. `_TARGET_STOP` (written, printed, painted, glowing ...) is checked only from the second word on. So participles, adverbs and prepositions ('printed', 'carved into the wood', 'about climate change') become the target.
- **Verb triggers** (reads/reading/says/spells): they need only a bearer noun somewhere in the preceding 40 characters, not the verb's subject. So 'a box reading comics' and 'a book of spells glowing' count as lettering.

These targets are exact=True, so `_quote_text` offers an Apply that quotes description, and the re-check then passes. The wrong spans also go into `rendered_spans`, which has two further effects. The critic accepts a rewrite quoting those words, with no `heuristic.rewrite_quote`. And `_negation` skips `ctx.rendered`, so a real negation inside such a span is no longer reported. Verifiers split between medium and high; the final severity is medium, because Apply is a visible, undoable click.
confirmed.failure_scenario:
On the default FLUX.1 Krea [dev]:
- 'A t-shirt with the words printed across the chest' gets Apply 'A t-shirt with the words "printed" across the chest'.
- 'A boy sitting on a box reading comics' quotes "comics".
- 'An ancient book of spells glowing on the altar' quotes "glowing".
- 'An old man with a newspaper reading without glasses by the fire' loses its negation warning. Instead, 'without glasses by the fire' is offered as lettering to quote.
confirmed.suggested_fix:
- Check the first word after a trigger against a description stop set: `_TARGET_STOP` plus participles and prepositions such as carved, etched, embossed, handwritten, into, about, by and overlay, and -ly adverbs.
- For verb triggers, require the bearer to be the verb's subject: directly before the verb, optionally with 'that' or 'which' between.
- Mark a lowercase target that is not all capitals as exact=False.
- Add negative cases to test_quoted_or_non_text_words_are_left_alone, and assert that `rendered_spans` is empty for them.

confirmed.failure_scenario:

merged_from: Text to render and rewrite lettering may run past an exact lettering end into description, unflagged
confirmed.title: Lettering accepted past an exact end: description passes as text to render
confirmed.description:
`_lettered` has a fallback that accepts words starting inside any rendered span and running on to the next clause break. It is meant for unquoted lettering whose end the rules had to guess.

`rendered_spans` discards `_Target.exact`, so the fallback also applies where the rules ended the lettering for certain at a stop word (in, on, above, and ...). Description after the lettering is then accepted:
- as text_to_render;
- in a quoted rewrite, which escapes `heuristic.rewrite_quote`.

Layer-1 lint skips quoted text, so nothing flags it. The result is also inconsistent: when the prompt already quotes the lettering, the same rewrite is dropped. This contradicts `_lettered`'s docstring ('Never the prompt's description') and CLAUDE.md's rule that a rewrite quoting description is flagged.
confirmed.failure_scenario:
On FLUX.1 Krea [dev], 'A diner at night, a neon sign that says OPEN in red letters above the door' has a rule span of exactly 'OPEN'.
- The rewrite '...reads "OPEN in red letters above the door".' is kept with no rewrite findings, and Use rewrite asks the model to letter the whole phrase.
- For '...says OPEN and a cat sleeps under it', text_to_render='OPEN and a cat sleeps under it' is kept.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Pass the rules' `exact` flag through with the spans (for example a `rendered_targets` function, or a third field). Allow the run-on fallback only for exact=False targets. Optionally let an exact span run on through further all-capital words, so 'OPEN IN 5 MINUTES' still passes. Add test_critic cases for both prompts above.

merged_from: A rewrite quoting the prompt's lettering with a different apostrophe is dropped whole as invented lettering
confirmed.title: Rewrite dropped as invented lettering when only the apostrophe or dash differs
confirmed.description:
`_check_rewrite` drops the whole rewrite when a quoted stretch is neither `_lettered` nor found by `locate`. Both comparisons fold only case and whitespace, so a straight apostrophe against a curly one, or a hyphen against an en dash, fails. The rewrite is then dropped with the note 'lettering the prompt does not ask for', which is false: it is the same lettering.

The check is also inconsistent. Changing 'Joe's Diner' to 'JOE'S DINER', a bigger visible change, passes. And the same module already folds ’ to ' in `_stem`. Curly-quoted prompts pasted from Word, macOS or iOS are ordinary input.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The prompt is 'A diner at night with a neon sign that says “Joe’s Diner”' and the critic's rewrite uses a straight apostrophe in "Joe's Diner". The result is rewrite=None and set_aside 'it puts "Joe's Diner" in quotation marks - lettering the prompt does not ask for.' The reverse case (straight in the prompt, curly in the rewrite) behaves the same, as does 24-7 against 24–7.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Apply a one-to-one `str.translate` table in both `_flat` and `locate` that folds ’‘ʼ′ to ', “”„ to " and –—− to -. Because each character maps to exactly one character, the returned offsets still index the original prompt. Optionally, when a match succeeds only after folding, keep the rewrite with a warning that the lettering's punctuation changed. Add tests for both directions.

merged_from: is_reorder casefolds pieces, so a 'pure reorder' may change case, including unquoted lettering
confirmed.title: is_reorder casefolds pieces, so 'Reordered' may change case of unquoted lettering
confirmed.description:
`_pieces` casefolds each piece and strips its end punctuation before comparing. Only QUOTED stretches are compared case-sensitively. So a candidate whose case changed throughout still passes as a pure reorder.

This contradicts `is_reorder`'s docstring ('pieces moved and nothing else'), the module docstring ('with any text to render unchanged') and the design notes ('the order and nothing else'). T5 and Qwen3 are case-sensitive: the verifier measured T5 at 25 tokens for the original and 37 for the upper-cased version. Unquoted sign text changes what gets lettered. On prose, the page falls back to the critic's `reordered` for the comparison's default-ticked Reordered row. test_critic.py:755 pins an upper-cased reorder as kept.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On Krea [dev], the prompt is 'Neon city at night, a sign that says Open Late, a woman in a Burberry trench coat'. The critic's all-caps reorder is kept. The Reordered grid row then renders an all-caps T5 prompt with the sign now reading OPEN LATE, and credits the difference to order alone.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Keep the case-insensitive permutation test, but once `is_reorder` accepts a candidate, rebuild `reordered` from the prompt's own original pieces in the candidate's order. The Reordered row is then the user's exact text, moved. Alternatively, drop the casefold and hold unquoted lettering from `rendered_spans` character for character. Update test_critic.py:755 and add an unquoted-sign case.

merged_from: Restated-finding span check drops issues about neighbouring words that do not overlap the finding
confirmed.title: Restated check drops issues whose quote merely sits near a finding
confirmed.description: `_restated` drops an issue when its located quote lies anywhere inside [finding.start-8, finding.end+8]. It never requires the quote to overlap the finding's words. The slack was meant to cover 'with no people,' against 'no people'. In practice it also swallows short, separate phrases next to any finding that has a span (negation, quote_text, order, repeated ...), and set_aside then says they repeated that finding. The test passes only because its kept issue quotes 'a shop sign', which reaches past the window.
confirmed.failure_scenario:
- Krea [dev]: 'A quiet street after the rain, no people, a shop sign that says Open Late.' Issues quoting 'a shop' ('What kind of shop?') and 'rain' ('Rain is vague') are both removed with '2 issues left out: they repeated the rule findings above (negation).'
- 'A quiet beach, no people, sunset' drops issues quoting 'beach' and 'sunset'.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Count a span match only when the quote overlaps the finding (issue.start < end and issue.end > start). Keep the ±8 slack only as a limit on how far past the finding the quote may run. Add a test with a short, non-touching quote inside the window, and assert that it is kept.

merged_from: A finding about characters (encoder.unknown_chars) counts as a finding about the words: on a Chinese prompt on FLUX.1, every quoted critic issue is dropped as 'repeated the rule findings above (unknown_chars)'
confirmed.title: encoder.unknown_chars spans make the critic's quoted issues vanish as 'restated'
confirmed.description:
`reported_spans` leaves out only encoder.cut and encoder.template_tail (`_NOT_ABOUT_WORDS`), because their spans mark where an encoder stops reading, not what the words mean. encoder.unknown_chars and encoder.control_token are about characters too, but their spans stay in.

On FLUX.1, T5 reads <unk> for nearly all of a CJK prompt. Up to 8 unknown runs then cover the whole text, so every quoted critic issue is dropped with set_aside '(unknown_chars)', whatever it is about. The same happens on English prompts to short quotes near a character T5 cannot read, such as { } or ~. These findings are info-level and sort late, so the model may not even have been shown them. (Cyrillic is barely affected: its unknown runs are single letters.)
confirmed.failure_scenario: On FLUX.1 Krea [dev], the prompt '夜晚的霓虹城市，一个撑红伞的女人走过一家商店，没有行人，胶片摄影' produces unknown_chars spans at (0,7), (8,22), (23,27) and (28,32). An issue quoting '没有行人', and another quoting the subject, are both removed with '1 issue left out: it repeated the rule findings above (unknown_chars).' 'a cat {sitting} on a mat' drops an issue quoting 'a cat' in the same way.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add encoder.unknown_chars to `_NOT_ABOUT_WORDS`, and consider encoder.control_token too. Better, limit the span check to rules whose spans are about meaning (guide.*, heuristic.*, encoder.weighting), and apply no slack to single-token spans. Add test_critic cases for the Chinese FLUX.1 prompt and the '{sitting}' prompt.

merged_from: Restated-by-wording patterns drop unrelated issues ('dress length is', 'emphasis') with a false 'repeated the rule findings above' note
The critic drops word-count issues when no word-count finding exists, and tells the user it 'repeated the rule findings above'
confirmed.title: Word-count and weighting patterns drop unrelated critic issues with a false note
confirmed.description:
Three problems in the 'restated' check:

1. **guide.words is always treated as reported.** `_restated` counts it as told whenever the guide has a word range (`words_measured`), even when no guide.words finding was reported. Its pattern matches any number followed by 'words', and 'length of' or 'length is'. So ordinary description (dress length, focal length, exposure length) and legitimate 'add N words' fixes are dropped.
2. **Negative-prompt findings suppress prompt issues.** `reported` includes findings on the negative prompt, so a weighting finding there drops prompt issues that mention 'emphasis', 'weight' or 'bracket'.
3. **The note is false.** set_aside says the issue 'repeated the rule findings above', naming a finding that may not be on the page at all.

Dropping length claims on in-range prompts is deliberate (design-notes 2346), but README:952 and CLAUDE.md describe only reported findings. The sources were rated low and medium. The higher is kept because this is a valid, sourced issue removed with a false reason on the default checkpoint.
confirmed.failure_scenario:
- Krea [dev], a 42-48-word prose prompt with no rule findings: 'The dress length is not specified', 'Give a focal length of 85mm' (citing G2, the camera sentence) and 'add 3 words on its glow' are all removed with '... repeated the rule findings above (word count).'
- Animagine with the negative '(worst quality:1.4), lowres': 'Give the expression more emphasis' is removed as '(weighting)'.
confirmed.suggested_fix:
- Narrow the guide.words pattern to claims about the prompt's own length.
- Build `reported` from prompt-field findings only, as `reported_spans` already is.
- When guide.words was not reported, word the note as 'it spoke to the prompt's length, which the check measured (N words, inside the range)'.
- Update README.md:952 and CLAUDE.md.
- Add tests where a focal-length issue and a negative-only weighting finding both leave prompt issues intact.

merged_from: Check reports a tag checkpoint's order as checked when the tag index lookup failed, and nothing in the response says the lookup failed
Unreachable tag index leaves order_checked true, so a skipped order check shows as passed
order_checked is True when the tag index is unreachable, so an out-of-order tag prompt reads as a passed order
confirmed.title: Order shown as checked when the tag-category lookup failed
confirmed.description:
`_tag_categories` catches every lookup failure (offline, 5xx, an unreadable reply) and returns None, the same value it returns when there was nothing to ask. Items past the 64-item cap are silently never asked about.

With no categories, `_place` gives each item the guide's own groups do not know the whole unknown range. Character, series and artist misorders therefore cannot be flagged, and `reorder_tags` returns None. Yet `order_checked` is computed from the spec, style and item count alone, so it stays True. PromptAnalysis has no field recording the failure. The page then draws the chain with no 'Not checked' note, and the summary can read 'nothing to flag'.

Offline, an out-of-order prompt and an in-order prompt get byte-identical answers. That is the misreading `order_checked` was added to prevent (design-notes 2141-2149, 'costs the order check'). Anima's artist_prefix check also stands down with no trace, and tests/test_api_analysis.py:242-245 pins order_checked=True offline. One verifier rated this low, on the grounds that CLAUDE.md sanctions the None fallback. Two rated medium, because the response hides the fallback; medium is kept.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Animagine XL 4.0 with Danbooru unreachable, prompt '1girl, green hair, firefly (honkai: star rail), masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres'. The answer is order_checked=true, no guide.order finding, reordered=null and encoders_detail=null. The panel shows the chain as checked and 'nothing to flag'. With the index reachable, the same prompt gets a guide.order finding and a reorder.
confirmed.suggested_fix:
- Have `_tag_categories` report why it returned None when the lookup was needed but failed, or when the list was cut at the 64-item cap.
- Add a `categories_detail` field (parallel to `encoders_detail`), or set order_checked False or partial in that case.
- Show 'Partly checked: the tag index was unreachable' under the chain, and 'order partly checked' in the summary. For Anima, say that the artist check did not run.
- Update test_api_analysis.py:242-245, and assert that the offline answer differs from an in-order online answer.

merged_from: Order reported as checked for newline- or fullwidth-comma tag lists the order rule never splits
A tag list separated by newlines (or Chinese commas) is read as tags but ordered as one item: order_checked is true, nothing is placed, and the whole prompt goes to Danbooru as one tag
confirmed.title: Newline- or fullwidth-comma tag lists read as tags but the order is never placed
confirmed.description:
`detect_style` splits pieces on ASCII commas, fullwidth commas and newlines, so a list written one tag per line, or with '，', reads as tags. `comma_items` splits on ',' only, so the same text is a single item. `_order` and `reorder_tags` then stop at fewer than 2 items, but `order_checked` still returns True.

The panel shows the documented order as checked with nothing flagged. That breaks CLAUDE.md's rule that order_checked is True only where a rule placed the prompt. `_suffix` compares the whole item, so it reports suffix tags as missing when they are present, and its Apply appends duplicates. Sending the whole text to Danbooru as one tag is harmless: the chips do the same. The sources were rated medium and low. Medium is kept because this breaks a stated rule and emits a false 'missing' suggestion.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On Animagine, 'masterpiece', 'safe', '1girl' on separate lines (fully reversed), or 'masterpiece，safe，1girl，smile', gives style tags, order_checked true, reordered null and no guide.order finding. The guide.quality finding also says 'The recommended finish is missing masterpiece, ...' even though it is present.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Return False from `order_checked` when `detect_style`'s pieces outnumber the comma items, so the page says 'Not checked'. Alternatively, treat '，' as a comma in both `comma_items` and the chips' split. Stop `_suffix` from reporting tags found as newline- or '，'-separated pieces, and from offering a duplicating Apply. Optionally add a guide-cited info finding that suggests ASCII commas. Add tests on Animagine for a newline list and a fullwidth-comma list.

merged_from: FLUX.1's 'English is the most precise language' is citable, linked to the BFL page the repo says contradicts it
schnell's first guide sentence (G1) says T5 stops at 256 tokens; the analyser reports 511 on the same page, and the critic may cite G1
The critic can cite guide sentences that the repo itself says are contradicted by their linked source (FLUX.1 'English is the most precise language', schnell's 256-token T5)
confirmed.title: Critic may cite guide sentences that their own linked source contradicts
confirmed.description:
Two guide sentences that the repo itself says are wrong are citable by the critic:

- **FLUX1_GUIDE's G5**, 'English is the most precise language.' guides.py:65-66 and design-notes 2162-2164 say BFL's current basics page contradicts it ('with the same level of quality'), so the rules leave it out. `sources_for` still makes it citable G5, linked to that same page.
- **SCHNELL_GUIDE's G1**: 'schnell's T5 encoder stops at 256 tokens, about 180 words'. The app passes no max_sequence_length, so FluxPipeline encodes 512. prompt_encoding reports 511, the README says 'T5 512 in this app', and guides.py:148-150 concedes the limit does not apply. schnell's analysis has no `words` key, so nothing sets such an issue aside.

The `unsourced` mechanism exists for exactly this (design-notes 2289-2295), but no Grounding sets it. The Krea [dev] 'photo language' precedent was fixed by removing the sentence from the prose. e7d2386 made both sentences citable.
confirmed.failure_scenario:
- FLUX.1-dev with a French or German prompt: 'Rewrite the prompt in English' citing G5 passes validate. The page shows it as 'G5 · Guide', linked to BFL's basics page, which says the opposite.
- schnell with a 200-word prompt: 'Cut the prompt to under 180 words' citing G1 is kept, while the Encoders row on the same panel shows T5 200/511 with no cut.
confirmed.suggested_fix:
- Remove 'English is the most precise language.' from `_FLUX1_PROMPT`; the lighter alternative is to list it in FLUX1_GUIDE's `unsourced`.
- Reword schnell's G1 to say this app encodes 512 tokens (BFL's reference stops at 256), or pass max_sequence_length=256 on schnell. Keep 'descriptive sentences, subject first, text in quotation marks' as its own citable sentence.
- Add a test that no citable sentence contains either phrase, and that no G sentence states a token limit different from the checkpoint's prompt_encoding budget.

merged_from: No G sentence is listed `unsourced`, yet many are the app's own UI statements or judgements, and they are numbered, cited and shown as the authors' guide
confirmed.title: App-written guide sentences are cited as the authors' guide
confirmed.description:
The prompt_sources docstring, the comment on `Grounding.unsourced` and design-notes 2289-2291 all say a guide sentence with no author behind it is listed `unsourced` and never citable. Every GROUNDING entry leaves `unsourced` empty.

About 25 citable G sentences are the app describing its own UI or giving its own judgement. Examples:
- Illustrious G9, 'masterpiece, newest is a practical starting tail, not an official fixed suffix' (design-notes 1474-1477: app-added), and G13, 'The Tags menu fills the long one.'
- Animagine G5/G6; Kohaku G4/G6/G10; WAI G4/G7; NetaYume G3/G7; NewBie G5/G6.
- ERNIE G2 (Expand) and G4 (the config's 2048).
- The fallback's G1, 'Unrecognised checkpoint.'
- Z-Image base G5, 'Tongyi strongly recommends a negative prompt', though its card calls one optional.

`build_context` tells the model these sources are 'from the checkpoint's authors'. `_issue` resolves them as source 'guide' with the author's URL, and the page shows 'Gn · Guide' linked there. The fallback's system message calls them authors' sources two lines before saying none are known. The sentences predate the commit as badge text; e7d2386 made them citable.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On Illustrious XL v2.0, the prompt '1girl, solo, looking at viewer, best quality' draws the issue 'end with masterpiece, newest', citing G9. The page shows 'G9 · Guide' linked to arXiv 2409.19946v1, presenting the app's own self-described unofficial suggestion as the authors' report.
confirmed.suggested_fix: List the app-voice sentences verbatim in each Grounding's `unsourced`, or move UI remarks out of the `prompt` prose into a hint that `sources_for` never reads. For the fallback, give the critic no G sentences, or drop the 'from the checkpoint's authors' wording when `sources.url` is None. Add a test that markers such as 'this app', 'Tags menu', 'Examples', 'Autocomplete', 'Expand' and 'not an official' never appear in a citable sentence.

merged_from: Cut message quotes the prompt's opening, not where reading stops, for unspaced CJK/Japanese text
confirmed.title: Cut message quotes the prompt's opening for unspaced CJK text
confirmed.description:
`_snippet` moves the start back to the beginning of the word that the cut splits. It treats every character as part of a word unless it is whitespace or an ASCII ',' or ';'. Unspaced Chinese or Japanese, including its 、，。 punctuation, therefore walks all the way back to index 0. The encoder.cut message then says reading stops at the prompt's first words, the opposite of what happens.

The finding's `start` is correct, so the page selects the right place; only the quoted text is wrong, and it is shown verbatim. The only test of this uses Latin text.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On Kohaku XL Zeta, a Japanese prompt repeated 3 times (282 CLIP tokens) is cut at offset 41. The message nonetheless says reading stops at "青い髪の少女が桜の木の下で...", the opening of the prompt. The same happens on FLUX.1 Krea (the CLIP-L info finding), Animagine, Z-Anime and NetaYume.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Treat Unicode punctuation (category P*) as a word boundary, and never move back across characters of scripts written without spaces (Han, kana, Hangul). Alternatively, move back only to the start of the token the cut falls in, or cap the move. Add a test with an unspaced CJK prompt, asserting that the snippet starts at or near the cut.

merged_from: A non-UTF-8 install marker makes ready() raise, failing /api/status on every poll; install never recovers
confirmed.title: A non-UTF-8 install marker makes /api/status 500 on every poll
confirmed.description:
`installed_server()` reads the marker with `read_text(encoding="utf-8")` and catches only OSError. UnicodeDecodeError is a ValueError, so it escapes. Two things then break:
- `ready()` raises instead of returning False, and the status route calls it with no guard.
- `install_server()` raises before reaching its branch that replaces an unfinished tree, so the install never recovers.

`verify_model`'s stamp read already catches (OSError, ValueError). This breaks CLAUDE.md's rule that supported()/ready() are 'file checks only, fit for /api/status'. It needs an outside cause, such as the marker being re-saved as UTF-16 by PowerShell 5.1's Out-File, or disk corruption.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The marker is re-saved as UTF-16 LE with a BOM. Every GET /api/status returns 500, so the page loses the model id, defaults, guide, hints and load state. Every critique returns 500 with a bare UnicodeDecodeError. This lasts until the user finds and deletes the marker by hand.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Catch (OSError, ValueError), or compare the raw bytes with `_recipe(key).encode("utf-8")`. An undecodable marker then counts as 'not installed' and the existing replace branch runs. Add a non-UTF-8 marker case asserting three things: `installed_server()` returns None, `ready()` is False, and `install_server()` replaces the tree.

merged_from: Cleanup in _run's finally can replace a finished critique with a PermissionError, and only the direct child process is stopped
confirmed.title: Critic cleanup can turn a finished critique into a 500 and orphan a server
confirmed.description:
`_run` hands the temp log file to the child as its stdout. `_stop` terminates, waits for and kills only the direct child: there is no job object and no process group. The outer finally's `log_path.unlink()` is unguarded, so an OSError there replaces the payload `_run` was about to return. If `_stop`'s second wait times out, `self._process` is never cleared.

The pinned llama-server has no children, so the default setup is safe. But `LOCAL_DIFFUSION_CRITIC_SERVER` is documented only as 'a llama-server of your own', and a shim, .bat or wrapper script is accepted. In that case the docstring's promises ('never leave a server running', 'the card is free before an image job is let in') fail.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On Windows, with the setting pointing at a .bat file or the venv trampoline: the chat completion returns 200, then `_run` raises PermissionError WinError 32 on the log file (5 of 5 runs). The route answers 500 and the log is left in %TEMP%. With a .bat, the real server also keeps listening after `_run` returns, which is when the gate opens. On Linux, a sh wrapper without exec is killed while llama-server stays up holding about 5.5 GiB until --sleep-idle-seconds passes.
confirmed.suggested_fix:
- Wrap the unlink in a try/except OSError and log the failure.
- Clear `_process` in its own finally.
- Stop the whole process tree: on Windows a job object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, or taskkill /T; on POSIX start_new_session=True with os.killpg.
- Document that the setting must be the llama-server binary itself.

merged_from: Unload and shutdown wait out a first-use tokenizer download, because prompt_encoding.unload() blocks on the lock that measure() holds across Hub fetches; Check itself runs that download on asyncio.to_thread
A tokenizer fetch holds prompt_encoding._lock over unbounded Hub I/O, so Unload and shutdown wait behind it
confirmed.title: Tokenizer lock held over unbounded Hub I/O blocks Unload and shutdown
confirmed.description:
`measure()` holds `_lock` across `_cached` -> `_load_tokenizer` -> `snapshot_download(local_files_only=False)`. That download's repo_info and list_repo_tree calls use huggingface_hub's default httpx client, which has timeout=None. `unload()` takes the same lock, and both the Unload route and lifespan shutdown await it. So they wait for any first-use Check's fetch, and wait forever if the connection stalls.

Knock-on effects:
- The Unload route updates `_load_state` only after these awaits. Meanwhile /api/status says 'ready' while the weights are already gone, and POST /api/model/load is a no-op.
- A load started in that window is relabelled 'unloaded' for its whole duration.
- The analyze and critique routes run `_analyse` via `asyncio.to_thread`, the non-daemon pool `_detached`'s docstring warns about, so interpreter exit also waits for a stuck fetch.
- The page disables neither Unload nor Check during a Check.

The lifespan comment states the rule this breaks. The sources were rated low and medium; medium is kept because the verifier demonstrated an indefinite stall under httpx's default timeout.
confirmed.failure_scenario: First Check on an uncached checkpoint over a stalled connection, then the user clicks Unload. Unload never answers, status keeps saying 'ready', and Load does nothing. Ctrl-C then hangs in lifespan, and a second Ctrl-C does not interrupt it, so the process has to be killed.
confirmed.suggested_fix:
- Give the analyser's Hub fetch a bounded timeout.
- Take `_lock` only around the `_tokenizers` lookup and insert. Load outside it, with a per-source in-flight guard and a generation counter so a load that lands after unload() is discarded.
- In the Unload route, set `_load_state` right after `try_unload` succeeds.
- Optionally run the analysis on `_detached`.

merged_from: Sheet pins the var:variant axis instead of giving it the rows when each version has exactly one image
confirmed.title: Sparse comparison sheets pin var:variant instead of giving it the rows
confirmed.description:
`chooseAxes` drops every listlike axis (one value per record) whenever anything else varies, and this happens before the VARIANT_AXIS splice. So when each version has exactly one loaded image, var:variant is removed. That is the case after starring one image per version and viewing with Favorites on, or after Delete unstarred. `reconcileAxes` then pins var:variant to its first value, and `renderSheet` hides the other versions.

This contradicts CLAUDE.md, the design notes and README 776-778 ('always take the rows when anything else varies'). The listlike drop predates the commit; the new variant rule was simply not ordered ahead of it.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A 3-version x 4-seed comparison. The user stars (original, seed 2), (reordered, seed 2) and (rewrite, seed 4), then views the run with Favorites on. The sheet reads '1 of 3 loaded · pinned to variant original'.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Exempt VARIANT_AXIS from the listlike filter, or find it in the unfiltered list before the splice. Add a Node check of `chooseAxes`, or a smoke step, for a sparse comparison.

merged_from: With the gallery's Favorites box ticked, a finished comparison opens as an empty sheet
A finished comparison opens an empty sheet while the gallery's Favorites tick is on
confirmed.title: A finished comparison opens an empty sheet while Favorites is ticked
confirmed.description: When the comparison job reports done, `showRun` sets the search box to run:<id> and calls setSheet(true), but it leaves the other gallery filters alone. `loadGallery` adds favorites=true whenever els.favOnly is ticked. The newly rendered images are not starred, so the sheet that CLAUDE.md says the comparison 'opens ... when done' shows 'Nothing matches'. The tick is not persisted, but it stays on for the session. One verifier rated this low (it recovers once Favorites is unticked); the other rated medium because it breaks a stated contract. Medium is kept.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The user ticks Favorites to browse starred images, checks a prompt and runs an 8-image comparison. The sheet opens on run:<id> with 0 cells, while the server holds all 8 images. The user has to notice and untick Favorites.
confirmed.suggested_fix: When a comparison opens its run, untick els.favOnly before `showRun` and say so in the sheet note, or give `showRun` a flag that omits favorites=true. Add a smoke-analysis step that ticks Favorites before runComparison and expects 8 cells.

merged_from: The documented comparison recipe (`stats --by prompt`) prints versions that cannot be told apart: prompts are cut to 37 characters, no key exists for the variant label, and rows sort by rate
confirmed.title: Documented 'stats --by prompt' comparison recipe cannot tell versions apart
confirmed.description:
README and the design notes present `python -m backend.stats --run <id> --by prompt --min 4` as the starred rate per version of a comparison. It cannot show that:

- `storage._GROUPS` has no key for the variables column, so `--by variant` exits 2.
- `_cell` cuts every value to 37 characters plus '...' and passes newlines through.
- Rows sort by rate, not by the order the versions were written.

Reorders, the case the comparison exists for, usually share their first 37 characters, so their rows print identically. XML prompts break the table across lines. Nothing else gives a rate per version: `--where 'run:X original'` is refused.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A 3-variant x 4-seed comparison of 'A woman in a red dress standing on a pier at dusk, ...' variants prints three rows that all read 'A woman in a red dress standing on a ...', at 100%, 50% and 25%. You cannot tell which version got 100%.
confirmed.suggested_fix:
- Add a 'variant' group key (json_extract(variables, '$.variant')) and change the recipe to `--by variant`.
- Fold whitespace and newlines to single spaces in `_cell`.
- Add a test that runs a prompt_variants grid, stars some cells and checks the versions can be told apart.

merged_from: No test pins that the critic is told the negative prompt as applied() runs it; build_context reading the raw request passes
confirmed.title: No test pins that the critic sees the negative prompt as applied() runs it
confirmed.failure_scenario: Under that regression, on Krea [dev] with no True CFG, the prompt 'A quiet street with no people' and negative 'people, crowds': the critic is told the negative runs and loses the 'No negative prompt runs' rule. With a long CJK negative, check_fits refuses 1,750-2,500-character prompts that do fit. No test fails.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add a `build_context` test with `request.negative_prompt` set and `applied` a copy with the negative removed. Assert that the user message has no '(it runs)' and the system message contains 'No negative prompt runs', and the reverse case. Optionally add a `check_fits` case with a long negative that is not sent.

merged_from: Typed CLIP control tokens in another case: SDXL's EOS reported as <unk>, BOS not flagged
confirmed.title: CLIP control tokens typed in another case go undetected
confirmed.description: CLIP's added special tokens are normalized=True, and the normalizer lowercases, so '<|EndOfText|>' tokenizes to EOS (49407). `_read` counts a control token only on an exact, case-sensitive match with the stored text. 49407 is also CLIP's unk id, so the typed EOS lands in the unknown-character branch ('has no token ... reads <unk>'), and a typed BOS in another case gets no finding at all. SDXL's CLIP-G pooled vector is taken at the first EOS.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On Kohaku, '1girl, <|EndOfText|>, <|STARTOFTEXT|>, solo' produces only an info finding claiming <unk>, and no encoder.control_token warning. On FLUX.1 Krea, '<|StartOfText|>' produces no finding.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Compare after the tokenizer's normalizer (normalize_str), or casefold for added tokens marked normalized=True. Never classify an id from `loaded.controls` as unknown. Add a mixed-case test.

merged_from: NetaYume negative prompt's report says it shares its budget with the system instruction
confirmed.title: NetaYume negative row claims to share its budget with the system instruction
confirmed.description: The spec's `role` ('shares its 256 tokens with the anime system instruction') is copied onto every EncoderReport. That includes the negative prompt, which is sent bare, matching Lumina2Pipeline, with a budget of 255. The page appends the role to every row. The test checks the role only on the prompt row.
confirmed.failure_scenario: NetaYume with a negative prompt at CFG 5: the negative row shows budget 255 with the note 'shares its 256 tokens with the anime system instruction'.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Set role to None for a negative reading when the spec's negative is 'bare', or add a separate negative_role. Extend the test.

merged_from: NetaYume system-prefix span is found in text.lower(), so offsets shift and the suggestion drops text
confirmed.title: NetaYume system-prefix rule finds its span in lower(), shifting offsets
confirmed.description: `_system_prefix` finds the prefix in `text.lower()` and uses that index on the original text. 'İ' lowercases to two code points, so the span shifts and the suggestion cuts the wrong characters. The suggestion also collapses every run of 2 or more whitespace characters in the whole prompt, including blank lines and spacing inside quoted lettering.
confirmed.failure_scenario: 'İİ You are an assistant ... prompts. 1girl' gets the Apply 'İİ Yogirl'. The prefix followed by ' 1girl, sign reading "OPEN    NOW"' has its quoted spaces collapsed.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Find the prefix with a case-insensitive `re.search` on the original text. Tidy whitespace only at the cut seams. Add tests.

merged_from: Negation rule warns on descriptive 'avoid' and on titles like 'Dr. No'
confirmed.title: Negation rule warns on descriptive 'avoid' and on titles such as 'Dr. No'
confirmed.description: avoid/avoiding is a negation head, so an action whose object is meant to be drawn is reported as an absence. On FLUX, where no negative prompt runs, that is a warn. `_particle` exempts only a lowercase 'no', so title-case 'No' is flagged. The fixed 3-word window can also cut a proper noun in half. The finding is advisory and has no Apply.
confirmed.failure_scenario:
On Krea [dev]:
- 'A cat trying to avoid the rain under a porch' gets warn 'avoid the rain'.
- 'A skier avoiding trees on a steep slope' is flagged the same way.
- 'The film Dr. No playing on a TV' gets warn 'No playing'.
- 'without ropes on El Capitan' is reported with the span 'without ropes on El'.
confirmed.suggested_fix:
- Remove avoid from the heads, or match it only as an imperative at a clause start.
- Skip a capitalised 'No' in mid-sentence or title case.
- Extend or trim the span so it never ends inside a run of capitalised words.
- Add near-miss tests.

merged_from: Order issues saying 'X before Y' are read as wanting X first, so issues that agree with the documented order are dropped as conflicting
confirmed.title: 'X before Y' order issues are read as 'X first' and dropped as conflicting
confirmed.description: The second `_WANTS` pattern treats '<part> ... before' as asking for that part first. Paired with a 'Start with the subject' issue, the two register as different wants, and every issue with a want is removed with 'asked for different things first'. Yet both follow the documented order the critic was given. The existing test covers only a real conflict.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On FLUX.1-dev, for 'Moody night photography, a small store with warm light, 35mm lens', the issues 'Start with the subject.' and 'Put the camera settings before the lighting.' are both removed with set_aside '(subject, camera)'.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Read 'X before Y' as a pairwise constraint. Count it as a conflict only when it contradicts another issue's want or the documented order. Add a test in which both issues survive.

merged_from: JSON reorder check accepts changed values (1.0 to 1, true to 1) with nothing moved
confirmed.title: JSON reorder check accepts 1.0 to 1 or true to 1 with no key moved
confirmed.description: `is_reorder`'s JSON branch requires equal Python values but different json.dumps output. Python treats 1 == 1.0 == True, so a candidate that only retypes a literal passes as a pure reorder. The same check also lets a real key move carry a retyped literal. Only klein has both a documented order and JSON prompts.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On klein, the prompt '{"subject": "a red fox", "count": 1.0, "style": "photo", "sharp": true}' gets a critic reordered version with "count": 1 and "sharp": 1. It is kept and offered as Reordered.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Require json.dumps(sort_keys=True) to be equal for both, and the unsorted dumps to differ. Optionally reject duplicate keys. Add tests.

merged_from: A wrapped rewrite with punctuation after the closing mark is dropped as invented lettering instead of unwrapped
confirmed.title: A wrapped rewrite with a period after the closing quote is dropped, not unwrapped
confirmed.description: `_unwrapped` needs the text to end exactly on the closing mark, so '"...".' is not recognised as a wrap. The fall-through then drops the rewrite as invented lettering, with a false note. CLAUDE.md says a wrapped rewrite is unwrapped, and verified.md records 4 of 19 real FLUX rewrites wrapped whole. A wrapped copy of the prompt with a trailing period is kept, quotation marks and all, with only a rewrite_quote warning.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On Krea [dev], prompt 'a cat on a sofa', rewrite '"A ginger cat curled up asleep on a worn velvet sofa".'. The result is rewrite None, with the note 'lettering the prompt does not ask for'.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Set trailing sentence punctuation aside before testing for the closer. If it is a whole wrap, return the inner text with the punctuation appended. Add tests for straight and curly quotes, and for a wrapped copy of the prompt.

merged_from: set_aside says the reordered version 'changed words' when only case or punctuation differ and nothing moved
confirmed.title: Reordered echo differing only in case or punctuation reported as 'changed words'
confirmed.description: When `is_reorder` returns False, the note is chosen by `_same`, which folds whitespace only. `is_reorder`'s `_pieces` casefolds and trims punctuation. So an echo with nothing moved but a changed case, a trailing '.', ';' for ',' or JSON spacing is told it 'changed words, not only their order'. The same case change is accepted silently when a piece does move.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On klein, the prompt 'neon city at night, a woman with a red umbrella, shot on film' echoed back upper-cased, or with a trailing '.', gets the false 'changed words' note.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Choose the note with `is_reorder`'s normalisation. Say nothing when the normalised pieces are equal. Extend the existing test.

merged_from: An over-length rewrite is dropped silently, with no set_aside line
README and design notes say everything validation removes is reported, but nulled parts (incl. text_to_render) are removed silently
confirmed.title: Validation removes over-length rewrites and nulled parts without a set_aside note
confirmed.description:
Two removals are not reported:
- `_prompt_text` returns None for a rewrite (or reordered) longer than MAX_TEXT.
- `_part` nulls parts that are not the prompt's words, and text_to_render that is not lettering.

Neither adds to set_aside, although README ('Anything left out is said so under the answer'), design-notes 2368-2369 and CLAUDE.md say it should. The page just drops the row. verified.md records text_to_render holding the scene description in most real runs. A rewrite or reordered identical to the prompt is also removed silently.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A 3,990-character prompt with a 4,070-character rewrite returns rewrite None and set_aside []. On Krea [dev], a text_to_render holding the scene description vanishes with no note.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add set_aside lines for over-length variants and for nulled parts the model filled, or narrow the README and design-notes wording to what is reported. Add assertions for both.

merged_from: The critic's `reordered` survives as any permutation, but the page offers it as 'the same words in the documented order'
confirmed.title: The critic's reordered can be any permutation but is offered as 'the documented order'
confirmed.description: `validate` enforces only `is_reorder` (same pieces, different sequence) and never compares the result with analysis.order or `reorder_tags`. The Use reordered tooltip still says 'the same words in the documented order', and `compareVariants` uses the critic's version as the Reordered row whenever Check has none. The real critic's reordered rarely survives (0 of 20 prose runs), so this is reachable but uncommon.
confirmed.failure_scenario:
- On klein, 'A woman with a red umbrella walks past a shop. Neon city at night. Shot on film.' gets a critic reorder that puts the subject last, and it is kept.
- On Animagine, a fully reversed tag list is kept as reordered, while Check itself flags that list with guide.order.
confirmed.suggested_fix:
- Where order_checked is true, keep the critic's reordered only if it matches `reorder_tags` or raises no guide.order finding.
- Elsewhere, reword the tooltip.
- Don't fall back to the critic's version in compareVariants when Check found nothing to move.

merged_from: Docs claim the two layers cannot link one guide sentence to two pages; for 7 guides they do
G sentences whose text names a different author page link to the guide's analysis URL; sentence_urls does not name them
confirmed.title: G sentences link to the guide's page even where their source is another page
confirmed.description:
`sources_for` gives every G sentence the guide's analysis['url'] unless `sentence_urls` names another page, and only Krea [dev] uses `sentence_urls`. Rule findings, by contrast, cite each entry's own url.

So one sentence links to two different pages across the two layers: 15 mismatches in 7 guides. For example, FLUX1's negation sentence links the technical page from a rule finding and the basics page from a critic cite. This contradicts prompt_sources.py:12-15 and design-notes 2285-2286.

Sentences that name their own source also link elsewhere:
- Illustrious G11 ('Their v0.1 card...') and G12 ('v2.0 release example') link to arXiv.
- Krea 2 G3/G4 link to prompting.md for technical-report claims.
- Z-Image G1 links to the card for a claim from discussions/8.

The test pins every Illustrious sentence to arXiv, with a false justification.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On FLUX.1-dev, 'A quiet street with no people': the rule finding links prompting_unified_technical, while a critic issue citing G4 (the same words) links prompting_unified_basics. On Illustrious, G11 opens arXiv for a sentence that quotes the v0.1 card.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Give sentences their own URL: from the cite-matching analysis entry, or via `sentence_urls` (use CivArchive for the v2.0 release post). Alternatively, reword the docstring and design notes. Replace the Illustrious assertion with per-sentence expectations.

merged_from: Sentence splitter fuses WAI's author negative-prompt sentence with an app statement, and leaves out-of-context fragments that the page shows alone as the cited words
confirmed.title: Sentence splitter fuses WAI's negative-prompt recipe with an app statement
confirmed.description: `_WAI_NEGATIVE` ends with a comma, so the interpolated prose has no full stop there. WAI's G8 is therefore the v17 card's recommendation fused with 'The card's weighted-prompt syntax and high-resolution refinement pass are not implemented by this text-to-image pipeline.' The fused sentence cannot be marked unsourced or linked separately, and the test checks only that the pieces rejoin. This is the only fused sentence across the guides. Other context-free fragments are a granularity trade-off, not a defect.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On WAI v17, a critic cite of G8 shows a tooltip that presents the app's statement about its pipeline as part of the card's words.
confirmed.suggested_fix: End the sentence in guides.py, for example with the recipe in quotation marks followed by a full stop, and leave `_WAI_NEGATIVE` unchanged. Add a test that no G sentence contains a new sentence start after a comma or semicolon.

merged_from: check_fits admits prompts whose answer cannot fit the window even with no thought (Greek, Korean, Japanese, Hindi), so a doomed critique runs on the GPU to the window's end and then 502s
estimate_tokens undercounts Greek, ZWJ emoji, hashes, base64 and escaped JSON/XML/tag copies, despite its docstring's 'erring long'; max_tokens then cuts answers that the window could hold
confirmed.title: Token estimate undercounts some scripts; check_fits and max_tokens misjudge fit
confirmed.description:
`estimate_tokens` counts non-ASCII text as UTF-8 bytes / 3 and claims to 'err long'. Against Qwen3's tokenizer (identical to the pinned GGUF) it gives: Greek about 0.70, base64 0.55, ZWJ emoji 0.80-0.88, Hindi 0.89, Korean about 1.0.

- `check_fits` scales by `_ESTIMATE_FLOOR` 0.6, which was sized for English's 1.57x overcount. For these scripts it admits prompts needing 1.4 to 2.4 times the 8k window, contrary to its docstring.
- `max_tokens` leaves less than the 2,048-token reasoning budget for Greek prompts from about 650 characters.

MEASURED includes none of these scripts. No wrongful refusals were found, and common scripts (Russian, Arabic, Thai, German) overestimate.
confirmed.failure_scenario:
- Krea [dev], a 2,500-character Greek prompt: check_fits computes 5,355 and admits it, but the real need is over 9,800 tokens. The server loads and thinks until the window is full, then answers 502 'ran out of tokens' about 30 s later (minutes under --fit), with image jobs waiting behind the gate.
- klein, a 1,000-character Greek prompt: max_tokens leaves about 1,650 tokens for thought, so a long thought is cut off with over 1,300 tokens of window unused.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Make the estimate a real bound per script, for example at least about one token per non-ASCII character, or count exactly with Qwen3's tokenizer.json fetched in prepare(). Fix the docstring, add Greek, Korean, Hindi, hex and base64 rows to MEASURED, and add an invariant test that admitted prompts fit.

merged_from: Typed chat-control text reaches llama-server raw, and on Qwen-encoder checkpoints the app's own RULE FINDINGS line carries it into the system turn
confirmed.title: Typed chat-control text reaches llama-server unescaped
confirmed.description:
The prompt and each finding message are embedded verbatim. llama-server renders the template and parses special tokens, so a literal <|im_start|>, <|im_end|>, <|endoftext|>, <think> or </think> becomes a Qwen3 control or reasoning token and can close or open turns.

- On non-Qwen checkpoints, Check does not flag these strings.
- On klein, Z-Image and Qwen-Image, the control-token finding quotes the token, and `build_context` copies that line into the system message. The app's own system turn therefore ends early.

The text is local and user-supplied, and the grammar and validation still apply, so the result is a misleading critique rather than a crash.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On Krea [dev], a pasted prompt containing <|im_end|> followed by a new system turn produces 5 im_start and 4 im_end tokens where the app built 3 and 2. On klein, a prompt ending in <|im_end|> puts that token inside the system message.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Escape these strings in all user and finding text sent to the server, for example by putting a zero-width joiner after '<'. Name tokens in finding lines without the literal text. Add a test. Optionally warn on Qwen chat markers whenever the critic is supported.

merged_from: An install interrupted mid-extract leaves its work directory behind, and nothing ever removes it
An exit during first-use llama.cpp extraction leaks a partial ~700 MB install directory that is never swept
Ctrl-C during the critic's first-use install can orphan a partial extraction tree that later installs never remove
confirmed.title: An interrupted first-use install leaks its extraction work directory
confirmed.description:
`install_server` extracts into `TemporaryDirectory(prefix=target.name+'-', dir=root)` on prepare's daemon thread. That work directory survives in two cases:
- a hard kill (the console window closed, taskkill);
- a normal exit while the daemon thread has a file open, where the atexit finalizer fails with WinError 32 or 145. This happens after a second Ctrl-C, or when the 30 s drain ends mid-extract.

A normal exit between zip members is cleaned up. Later installs remove only `target`, never '<target>-*' siblings. So each interrupted attempt leaks up to about 744 MB under HF_HOME/local-diffusion/llama.cpp, unlike .part downloads, which are cleared. The single_file and anima/netayume/newbie converters share the pattern.
confirmed.failure_scenario: First critique on Windows: the user closes the console during extraction. 'b11206-win-cuda-13.4-x64-XXXX', a partial tree, survives the next successful install. The verifier's run left 7 of these beside the published tree.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Inside the existing WeakFileLock, rmtree stale '<target>-*' directories before extracting, or use a fixed work path cleared before use. Add a test that plants a stale sibling. Consider the same sweep for the converters.

merged_from: The GGUF hash-mismatch advice 'delete it and retry' does not recover on a symlinked HF cache (WSL/Linux)
confirmed.title: GGUF hash-mismatch advice 'delete it and retry' loops on a symlinked HF cache
confirmed.description: The error message names the snapshot pointer. On WSL or Linux, where the Hub cache uses real symlinks, deleting the pointer leaves the blob. hf_hub_download then relinks the same corrupted blob without downloading, so the failure repeats, with a 4 GB rehash each time. Windows without symlinks does recover. This needs a corrupted blob of exactly the pinned size.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Under WSL, the cached Qwen3-4B-Q8_0 blob is corrupted at the right size. Every retry after deleting the named file gives the same 502.
confirmed.suggested_fix: On a hash failure, retry once with force_download=True. Alternatively, name path.resolve() (the blob) in the message.

merged_from: A LOCAL_DIFFUSION_CRITIC_MODEL that is a symlink is shown under its blob hash
confirmed.title: A symlinked LOCAL_DIFFUSION_CRITIC_MODEL is labelled with its blob hash

confirmed.title: A configured critic server that fails to start returns a bare 500
confirmed.description: An OSError from `_spawn`'s Popen is not wrapped as CriticError. So the route answers 500 with a raw WinError, contrary to `_prompt_failure`'s docstring ('a server that did not start' is a 502), and the message never names LOCAL_DIFFUSION_CRITIC_SERVER. `prepare()` accepts any path that passes is_file().

merged_from: The keyless /v1/models 401 probe does not verify which server answered; a process that takes the port gets the prompt and the key, and writes the answer
confirmed.title: The 401 probe does not prove the listener is the critic's own server
confirmed.description:
The port is exposed in a race:
- `_free_port` closes its probe socket before llama-server binds.
- The port is on the command line, which the code itself says other local users can read.
- `_wait_until_healthy` accepts any 200 while the child is merely alive.
- The keyless /v1/models 401 check filters out only well-behaved strangers.

A process that binds the port first and refuses keyless requests receives the prompt and this start's Bearer key, and can supply an answer that passes validate(). The design notes overstate the guard. Exploiting it needs a hostile co-resident account racing a sub-second window, which is realistic on WSL/Linux.
confirmed.failure_scenario: An attacker scans the process list, binds 127.0.0.1:<port> about 15 ms after spawn, and answers health with 200, keyless requests with 401, and the keyed chat with its own JSON. The critique returns the attacker's rewrite, and the attacker has logged the key and the prompt.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Before sending anything keyed, confirm that the listening socket belongs to the child's PID. On Linux, prefer a Unix socket in a 0700 directory. Correct the comment and the design notes.

merged_from: askCritic re-checks nothing after its pre-check await, so Generate and Expand stay unheld during the pre-check and a Check click cancels the critique without saying so
confirmed.title: Critic pre-check holds nothing, and a Check click during it drops the critique
confirmed.description:
When the check is stale, `askCritic` awaits `checkPrompt` first and sets `critiquing` only afterwards. During that pre-check:
- Generate, Run grid, Expand and Unload stay live, and startJob does not refuse.
- Nothing tests busy or expandingPrompt again after the await.
- A Check click supersedes the epoch, and askCritic returns with no critique and no message.

The server's guards (the 409s and the gate) prevent any GPU overlap.
confirmed.failure_scenario:
- ERNIE, the prompt edited after a check, Ask the critic, then Expand clicked during a slow pre-check: both editor actions are in flight together.
- Generate during the pre-check: the critique comes back 409.
- Check during the pre-check: the critique is silently never sent.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Set `critiquing` before the pre-check, or re-check the guards after it and say why the critique was not sent. Disable Check while the pre-check runs.

refuted.title: The real-tokenizer test cannot verify Qwen-Image's window or ERNIE's 2047 budget, so REAL leaves them out and every case skips on the machine that has those tokenizers
refuted.area: gap1:Linux and WSL coverage, run for real, offline. Every reviewe
refuted.why:
The finding describes the real-tokenizer test correctly, but the consequence it draws from that is wrong.

What is true (I reproduced it):
- The body of test_real_tokenizers_agree_with_the_pipelines_own_truncation (tests/test_prompt_encoding.py:891-902) does not account for Qwen-Image's window. It computes `kept` as a plain truncation to `limit` and never applies `[drop_idx:][:max_sequence_length]`.
- Its 700-word LONG prompt is too short to reach ERNIE's budget.
- So Qwen-Image and ERNIE could not be added to REAL (lines 863-872) as the test stands. With stand-in cached tokenizers (nothing downloaded):
  - Qwen-Image's spec over krea's cached Qwen3-VL tokenizer gives len(read)=546 against content=1058, so line 902 would fail. A window-aware replication (kept[34:][:512]) agrees with pe (546 positions, budget 512).
  - ERNIE's spec over the cached pe_tokenizer counts LONG at 1400 tokens against a 2048 limit, so cut is None and line 900 would fail.

What is false:
- "A regression in the window arithmetic of `_read` would pass everywhere" is wrong. test_qwen_image_keeps_a_window_after_its_system_turn_and_loses_the_tail_first (line 312) runs on the fake Qwen tokenizer and asserts the exact budget, `QWEN_IMAGE_PREFIX_TOKENS + QWEN_IMAGE_SEQUENCE - prefix`, plus the template-tail position. I simulated three regressions with a pytest plugin that wraps pe._read: window dropped, window off by one, and window[0] zeroed. Each time that test failed (1 failed, 119 passed). A broken Qwen-Image window count therefore does not ship green.
- "The design-notes numbers are held by no test" is also wrong:
  - ERNIE's 2047 is asserted directly by test_the_remaining_families_budgets (line 389), on a fake tekken tokenizer with model_max_length 2048 and one special token.
  - Line 820-823 checks that the installed ERNIE pipeline truncates with no max_length.
  - Lines 787-796 hold Qwen-Image's constants (start_idx 34, tokenizer_max_length 1024, sequence 512, max_length expression) to the installed diffusers source.
  - The 34-token count of the shared QWEN_SYSTEM_PREFIX on a real Qwen tokenizer is pinned by the Krea 2 REAL case (budget 507 = 512 + 34 - 5 - 34).
- design-notes.md:2054-2055 says "builder A matched" these budgets. That describes a manual check, not a claim that a test holds them. CLAUDE.md says only that the real-tokenizer cases skip when nothing is cached.
- On this Windows machine all 8 REAL cases run and pass: 120 passed with no skips in test_prompt_encoding.py. Only the WSL part of "every case skips on the machine that has those tokenizers" is plausible, because wsl/env.sh keeps a separate ext4 HF cache. It is not load-bearing.

What is actually left without a test is narrow: real-tokenizer agreement for the Qwen2.5-VL and ERNIE (Ministral) tokenizer files themselves, meaning their offsets and ERNIE's real special-token count. The arithmetic, the constants and the shared Qwen prefix count are all pinned. No failure the finding describes is reachable undetected.
